Photo by Antranik Tavitian/Getty Images)

House Democrats introduced a resolution Wednesday calling on Congress to withhold support for artificial intelligence (AI) companies if they go bankrupt as polling shows Americans largely oppose AI development on the eve of the midterm elections

The simple House resolution states that Congress would oppose any measure that would rescue insolvent AI-relate
news.originalContent:
Photo by Antranik Tavitian/Getty Images)

House Democrats introduced a resolution Wednesday calling on Congress to withhold support for artificial intelligence (AI) companies if they go bankrupt as polling shows Americans largely oppose AI development on the eve of the midterm elections

The simple House resolution states that Congress would oppose any measure that would rescue insolvent AI-related firms or shield senior executives from accountability for “reckless conduct that contributed to the failures of such firms.” Democratic Reps. Greg Casar of Texas and Maxine Waters of California introduced the resolution; a simple House resolution just expresses the sentiment of the House of Representatives and is not legally binding, meaning it does not require Senate or presidential approval.

The document states AI firms should “wind down or reorganize” through ordinary bankruptcy processes, administer resolution processes that promote competition, help workers and prioritize pension and retirement fund holders. It states that senior executives found to have taken excessive risk or acted unlawfully should “be held fully accountable under civil and criminal law.” (RELATED: Senators Not Keen On Banning AI From Surpassing Humans Despite Alarm Bells)

BREAKING: House Democrats have preemptively introduced a resolution to stop the federal government from bailing out AI companies in the event of the industry collapsing. The bill says these companies should be subjected to the ordinary bankruptcy process.

Technology companies are increasingly relying on outside investors, financial guarantees and complex financing arrangements to fund their data center expansion. Those arrangements could leave substantial obligations outside conventional debt disclosures, making it difficult to determine who bears the risk if anticipated AI profits fail to materialize.

S&P estimates that Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Oracle, Meta and SpaceX will collectively spend more than $7 trillion on AI-related capital expenditures between 2025 and 2030.

The largest tech companies in the U.S. were expected to borrow a record $420 billion in 2027 to finance the AI boom on Wall Street. Debt issuance was projected to rise 60% from 2026 levels as companies pour money into data centers, chips and other AI infrastructure, Goldman Sachs data found. Investors have grown concerned about how much additional debt will hit the market as companies rush to construct the infrastructure needed to compete in AI.

Major AI chipmakers such as Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom have expressed interest in investing up to $5 billion collectively in Meta while it seeks billions to fund its expanding AI infrastructure. These investments provide an opportunity to benefit financially from the expansion of AI infrastructure, although there is potential risk involved if demand for AI infrastructure slows.

An ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll from Oct. 21 found that 57% of Americans believe AI is bad for society, while 42% viewed it favorably. Most U.S. adults, 64%, said AI is developing too quickly, according to a survey conducted by The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research.

news.originalContent:
(Credit: Youtube; O’Keefe Media Group)

A prosecutor in Minnesota charged journalist James O’Keefe and conservative activist Cam Higby with felony unlawful voting Wednesday.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty also announced the state is charging both of them with identity theft. Both charges are punishable by up to five years in prison.

O’Keefe posted a video in August showing him and Higby entering Minneapolis polling stations on the day of the state’s primary election while wearing Islamic garb and using hidden cameras to record their interactions. Prosecutors argue such conduct applies to the law, which forbids the attempt to obtain a ballot by impersonating a registered voter.

O’Keefe spoke to poll workers in fake accents, while the pair made references to Muslim culture and Higby wore black garments covering his face and head. (RELATED: Senior White House Official Placed On Leave After Trashing Trump In Sting Operation)

A liberal prosecutor elected in 2022, Moriarty claimed at a news conference Wednesday that the charges were unrelated to the pair’s political views or the perception that their behavior and disguises were derogatory or offensive.

James Edward O’Keefe, 42, and Cam Higby, 26, both face felony charges of unlawful voting and identity theft. Polling places are the heart of our democracy. Any attempt to disrupt or deceive our election workers will not be tolerated. Watch: https://t.co/LH1Q5m224J https://t.co/NMPizpONcN

Moriarty cited evidence that O’Keefe posted a video documenting his interactions with poll workers, during which he and Higby discussed their goal of drawing attention to Minnesota’s voter-vouching law, according to the criminal complaints reviewed by the Daily Caller.

The law allows a registered voter to vouch for the residency of up to eight other voters who have recently moved, permitting them to cast ballots in precincts where they have not yet registered.

Moriarty further alleged in a Wednesday press release that O’Keefe “intentionally misrepresented their identities in applying for ballots.”Neither complainant alleges they cast their votes.

Separately, Moriarty has faced repeated criticism over her approach to juvenile offenders, particularly her aversion to incarceration, according to a Minnesota Star Tribune report.

Moriarty has also faced public criticism from members of her own party over her handling of serious violent-crime cases, including the 2023 murder of Zaria McKeever. Two teenage brothers, then 15 and 17, carried out the killing after McKeever’s ex-boyfriend, Erick Haynes, the father of her young child, allegedly gave them a gun and directed them to confront her new boyfriend. The younger brother, Foday Kamara, fired the fatal shots.

After entering office, Moriarty reversed an earlier push to prosecute the brothers as adults and offered them juvenile plea deals involving roughly two years in a correctional facility, followed by probation until age 21, in exchange for their testimony against Haynes and others, according to an MPR News report.

The older brother accepted the offer, while McKeever’s family strongly opposed the deals as inadequate. (RELATED: Independent Journalist Cam Higby Puts Anti-ICE Signal Group Live On-Air. They Aren’t Pleased.)

Democratic Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison also criticized the proposed outcomes as disproportionate, according to The Associated Press report.

After Moriarty declined to refer the case to Ellison’s office, Democratic Gov. Tim Walz invoked a rarely used statutory authority April 6, 2023, to transfer the case to the attorney general over Moriarty’s objections.

The move was the first such reassignment without local consent in roughly 30 years. Moriarty criticized the intervention as undemocratic.

Moriarty announced she would not seek reelection and told the Minnesota Star Tribune in August 2025 interview that she wanted to spend her remaining time in office focused on her work rather than campaigning.

🚨️️️️️️Calling all Election Judges, County Clerks, Poll Workers, and Watchers! Are you serving in the upcoming election? We want to connect with you to help ensure transparency and integrity in the electoral process. Send us a DM with your name, contact info, and the best time to reach you. You can also reach us on SIGNAL at 9144919395 or email us at tips@okeefemediagroup.com.

Higby responded to the news that Moriarty was pursuing felony charges against him in a post with a GiveSendGo link on X, writing, “I showed how Minnesota allows cheating in elections. Now they want to TAKE MY RIGHT TO VOTE AWAY. This is lawfare. They want to scare all independent journalists who may challenge them. This is FASCISM.”

The Trump administration has been pressing Minnesota and other states to turn over voter rolls containing sensitive personal information, arguing that federal access to the records is necessary to combat election fraud.

On Wednesday, the Daily Caller exclusively reported that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested 13 noncitizens accused of voter fraud ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: ICE Drops New Batch Of Illegal Immigrants Accused Of Voter Fraud Ahead Of Midterms)

The effort has fueled a broader national debate over election security and federal access to state-run voter registration systems.

The Daily Caller reached out to both O’Keefe and Higby for comment and did not receive a response in time for publication.

news.originalTitle: Trump Eyes New Iran Blitz After Midterm Elections
news.title: Trump Eyes New Iran Blitz After Midterm Elections
news.originalSummary:
(Photo by U.S. Central Command via Getty Images)

The Trump administration has privately warned several Gulf Arab governments to prepare for another intensive American military campaign against Iran following the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

U.S. forces are reinforcing Israel’s missile defenses, restocking weapons and shifting troops away from exposed bases as preparations for another confrontation
news.summary:
(Photo by U.S. Central Command via Getty Images)

The Trump administration has privately warned several Gulf Arab governments to prepare for another intensive American military campaign against Iran following the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

U.S. forces are reinforcing Israel’s missile defenses, restocking weapons and shifting troops away from exposed bases as preparations for another confrontation
news.originalContent:
(Photo by U.S. Central Command via Getty Images)

The Trump administration has privately warned several Gulf Arab governments to prepare for another intensive American military campaign against Iran following the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

U.S. forces are reinforcing Israel’s missile defenses, restocking weapons and shifting troops away from exposed bases as preparations for another confrontation accelerate, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday, citing people briefed on the discussions. President Donald Trump has not officially approved an operation but is leaning toward attacks on Iranian infrastructure and nuclear facilities, the outlet reported, citing people familiar with his thinking.

Trump publicly raised the prospect of renewed hostilities at a campaign rally in Florida on Friday.

“We may do another little Epic Fury, or they’ll agree,” Trump said, according to a rally transcript.

No attacks will happen before the midterm elections, the White House previously told the Daily Caller News Foundation. However, it never said strikes would not happen after the elections are finished.

The warnings were conveyed through diplomatic and military channels to several Gulf governments. American and Israeli planners are weighing an offensive intended to weaken Tehran and pressure its leaders to negotiate, according to the Journal. (RELATED: Signs Point At New And More Deadly Iran War On The Horizon)

(Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP via Getty Images)

“The forces pulling matters toward another round of war are much stronger than the forces pushing back,” Trita Parsi, executive vice president of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, previously told the Daily Caller News Foundation.

The warnings follow an exclusive report revealing that American military operations against Iran could rapidly intensify, according to a senior military official who spoke to the DCNF.

“Things are about to get spicy,” the senior military official told the DCNF.

The Pentagon is sending another Patriot air defense system from Texas to Israel, the Journal reported, citing flight-tracking records and two officials familiar with the transfer. U.S. bombers and fighter jets are also being prepared for potential strikes, officials told the outlet.

Approximately 9,000 additional sailors and Marines began deploying aboard the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and USS Makin Island amphibious ready group, potentially bringing the regional American naval presence to three aircraft carriers and more than 20,000 personnel, the Associated Press reported on Oct. 1, citing an anonymous U.S. official.

Another carrier strike group and Marine expeditionary unit could join approximately 20 American warships in the Middle East in November, although some vessels may rotate out, the Journal reported.

The White House declined to discuss potential military operations while insisting Iran must never obtain nuclear weapons, the Journal reported. Trump has previously said there would be no fresh American attack before the midterms, according to the outlet.

(Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP via Getty Images)

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is also pressing for renewed strikes, with Israeli officials preparing targets for another operation, the Journal reported. Netanyahu reportedly views military pressure as a way to further erode the Iranian regime’s power.

The possible offensive would follow months of American sanctions and a naval blockade that have squeezed Iran’s oil exports and trade.

The American naval blockade has prevented Iranian crude tankers from successfully escaping enforcement in the Gulf of Oman since July 12, leaving at least 53 oil-laden tankers clustered along Iran’s coastline as of Oct. 27, according to United Against Nuclear Iran.

Washington also imposed additional sanctions on foreign shipping agents, cargo vessels and financial facilitators involved in Iranian trade as part of its campaign to cut off Tehran’s oil revenue, according to the Treasury Department.

The conflict had cost the United States an estimated $47.1 billion by mid-October, including approximately $29 billion in expended weapons, according to estimates shared with lawmakers and described by the Journal. That figure excludes damage to American bases.

However, the war’s true cost is likely substantially higher, as Iranian strikes damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at American military bases across eight Middle Eastern countries, according to the Pentagon inspector general.

The watchdog also documented approximately $184 million in damage to U.S. diplomatic facilities, while the cost of repairing damaged military infrastructure remains uncalculated, according to the report.

Meanwhile, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has identified no repairs or reconstruction at Iranian nuclear facilities damaged in the 2025 and 2026 attacks, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told the United Nations Security Council on Tuesday.

However, Iran has not granted inspectors the access required to verify its nuclear material, including approximately 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium, Grossi told the Security Council. Inspections are continuing at the Bushehr nuclear power plant, according to Grossi.

(Photo by U.S. Central Command via Getty Images)

Iran still holds hundreds to thousands of missiles and is assembling new ballistic weapons from stockpiled components, the Journal reported. Tehran has threatened to strike economic and civilian targets throughout the Gulf if the U.S. attacks again.

Those threats come as Washington and its regional partners work to replenish air defense interceptors expended during earlier Iranian attacks. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: The Iran War Is Going To Go Ballistic After Midterms)

“Otherwise, at the moment, the U.S. has a winning hand through maintaining sanctions and the blockade. It should stay the course,” Behnam Ben Taleblu, senior director of the Iran program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told the Journal.

Regional mediators are still attempting to revive negotiations, but Washington and Tehran remain divided over the nuclear program and conditions for renewed talks.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Former St. John’s star RJ Luis Jr. was granted an injunction by a Baton Rouge, La., court Wednesday, making him temporarily eligible to play for LSU.

The injunction stops the SEC from being able to impose penalties on the LSU basketball program for having Luis on its roster, The Advocate reported.

A preliminary injunction hearing is set for Nov. 13, for which representatives for LSU and the SEC will be present, but until then Luis is able to practice and play games for the Will Wade-led program.

During that time frame, Luis would be able to play in three of LSU’s games, including the season opener against LSU New Orleans on Nov. 3, a Nov. 6 game against Texas Southern and a Nov. 9 matchup against Louisiana Tech.

Luis’ attorney, Tony Clayton, told The Advocate that “he can practice, he can play games, whatever, until the 13th.”

The ex-Red Storm star was named Big East Player of the Year in 2025 as part of the conference regular-season and tournament-winning squad. Luis made the decision to forgo his remaining eligibility and enter the NBA draft in 2025, but went undrafted before eventually signing a two-way deal with the Jazz.

He later signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Celtics.

Luis committed to playing at LSU after he was recruited by Wade, but the NCAA resisted letting Luis regain his college eligibility since he had decided to turn pro and did not follow NCAA protocols for retaining his eligibility by withdrawing from the draft.

The SEC has rules that prevent teams from adding players who had major professional experience. In September, it updated them to grant the commissioner the power to suspend coaches, fine schools up to half of their sport’s budget and restrict voting privileges on conference matters.

A petition filed by Clayton and attorney Elliot Abrams called on the state judge to prevent the SEC and conference commissioner Greg Sankey from penalizing LSU if Luis was put on the Tigers roster.

Clayton told The Advocate that it amended the lawsuit to include the SEC, Sankey and the LSU Board of Supervisors in order to take away any possible obstacle preventing Luis from playing for the Tigers.

Clayton has referred to the SEC commissioner as “Kim Jong” Sankey in several media interviews and told the Louisiana publication that the filing was due to the “commissioner’s actions and the commissioner’s threat.”

“The reason why we brought LSU into the suit is because LSU is being threatened by Mr. Sankey,” Clayton said. “LSU is a great institution. Coach Wade is a good guy, a good coach, but both of them need to be forced to allow RJ to play basketball since he’s obviously qualified. And not have the threat of the SEC, which is threatening LSU. In effect, stopping coach Will Wade from letting this kid exercise his fundamental right to play basketball.”

Luis averaged 18.2 points and 7.2 rebounds per game during his final season at St. John’s in 2024-25.

news.originalContent:

The 49ers’ reunion with DeForest Buckner came with a parting of ways.

San Francisco pulled off a trade to bring back the veteran defensive lineman Tuesday, sending a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Colts six years after dealing him to Indianapolis.

But making room for a familiar face meant showing someone else the door.

To accommodate Buckner on the roster, the star-studded team had to clear a spot. Jack Jones was the casualty.

The 49ers released the cornerback Wednesday, ending his stint on the team after seven games.

Jones’ release followed a difficult outing in Sunday’s 29-20 loss to the Falcons, which ended the 49ers’ unbeaten start.

Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. repeatedly picked on Jones, who was beaten in coverage multiple times and committed a costly pass-interference penalty that helped keep a Falcons drive alive.

The performance capped Jones’ brief stint in San Francisco, where he recorded 11 tackles and three passes defensed in seven games without making a start.

It was a reduced role for the veteran, who started 17 games for the Dolphins last season.

The 28-year-old recorded 77 tackles, six passes defensed and an interception in Miami before signing a one-year deal with the 49ers in April.

Jones stood out with the second-team defense during training camp before a hand injury cut short his appearance in the 49ers’ preseason opener against Tennessee.

San Francisco became his fourth NFL stop in five seasons, following stints with the Patriots, Raiders and Dolphins.

A fourth-round pick by New England in 2022, Jones showed promise as a rookie with two interceptions, including one returned for a touchdown.

But his Patriots tenure ended with his release in November 2023 after a team suspension and consecutive games in which he was benched.

Jones went on to play for the Raiders and Dolphins, accumulating eight interceptions across his first four seasons and returning four for touchdowns.

Buckner returns to a 6-1 team navigating injuries to key players, including Nick Bosa and Mike Evans, with other roster needs in focus ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

The 49ers return from their bye to host the Raiders on Nov. 8, two days before the deadline.

LA’s troubled utility has delivered a familiar lesson along with its water and power: Government has almost no incentive to spend other people’s money wisely.

Indeed, the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) has stuck ratepayers with costs that good financial stewards would not have abided.

These include far-left climate fancies that do near-zero to alter global temperatures — and, as The California Post reported this week, extravagant labor expenses.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

The Post found that LADWP shelled out a whopping $3.84 million to its five highest-paid employees in 2025; all five received more in overtime than in regular pay.

One worker took in more than $779,000, another banked more than $505,000 just in OT, and 114 employees collected more than $500K apiece.

Meanwhile, ratepayers’ bills are soaring.

Customers point to opaque costs that jump, sometimes by multiples, for no apparent reason.

That’s why Micah Reed, a San Fernando Valley resident with a $3,322.01 LADWP bill, gathered more than 39,000 signatures on a change.org petition to request an independent audit, along with summer rate relief.

Those are reasonable asks.

And LADWP is not alone in freely spending ratepayers’ money.

The California Post reported on Wednesday that the Santa Clara Valley Water District will pay three CEOs (former, interim and incoming) simultaneously for a portion of next year — at a combined two-month cost of $840,000, before benefits.

Yikes. How bad has a board’s management been when it sticks ratepayers with three overlapping salaries for the same top position?

One former Santa Clara water board member even called the tripling up “funny” and likened it to a sitcom. (We’re not LOLing.)

Meanwhile, officials in LA are just as patronizing.

LADWP commission president Allan Marks gave a half-hour monologue at Tuesday’s commission meeting before letting residents speak.

The spiel covered electricity costs, heat waves and conservation tips; one resident dubbed it “the 30-minute mansplaining.”

And no wonder: It’s a bit rich to urge further resident conservation while the commission itself spends lavishly.

After all, residents need energy for daily life, and there’s only so much heat people can take on triple-digit days.

LADWP has defended its bloated compensation as necessary to staff and run the agency, citing storms, heat, fires and hiring troubles.

But businesses that shrugged off similar (and often predictable) costs in the private sector would not survive long.

Instead of lectures, LADWP would do well to deliver transparency, cost savings — and the audit thousands of customers want.

Enough with the wanton spending of other people’s money.

CHICAGO — Mike Brown said he’s waiting for the Knicks to get back “on track” before incorporating some of the younger players — specifically Mo Diawara and Pacôme Dadiet.

“It’s tough because going into the season early on, one of [the] things I wanted to experiment with is playing 10 or 10 ½ guys [as my rotation],” Brown said. “And Mo is in that mix. Mo and Pac. Give them different opportunities at different times. And we experimented with different stuff and our players not getting it done caused us to start off a little slow.

“So to get us on track, we’re going to hold the fort down with a veteran group of guys. Hopefully we get to the point sooner than later that I can start throwing those [young] guys out there.”

The Knicks lost their first three games before blowing past the Pistons on Tuesday, a rough beginning for the defending champs.

Brown, meanwhile, has warned in his news conferences, at least twice, that the bench rotation is fluid.

Spots can be won or lost. The coach proved it already by benching Andre Drummond, a demotion that only lasted about a half against the Magic. Still, Brown’s nine- to 10-man rotation had been fairly consistent heading into Wednesday against the Bulls, with the one wrinkle being Tyler Kolek’s inclusion because Jose Alvarado missed three straight games with an ankle sprain.

With everybody healthy, it looked like this:

PG: Jalen Brunson, Alvarado

SG: Mikal Bridges, Miles McBride, Jordan Clarkson

SF: Josh Hart, Landry Shamet

C: Karl-Anthony Towns, Drummond

Notably absent from virtually any playing time was Diawara, a rangy forward who was a bit of a revelation as a second-round pick last season but lost his rotation spot before the playoffs. Diawara earned a new contract — four years, $11.3 million (only half guaranteed) — but not more playing time.

Diawara’s would-be minutes were going to Clarkson, the rotation’s 10th man. However, Brown only went with nine players in Tuesday’s victory over the Pistons — leaving Clarkson with his first DNP.

“Our starting five is what it is,” Brown said. “But everybody else after that, until we find something that’s working consistently, I’m going to try to give different guys opportunities.”

In the bigger picture, the rotation underscores how the Knicks weren’t created through the draft. Following Mitchell Robinson’s defection to Beantown, they’re down to just one homegrown pick as a rotation player — McBride. Kolek, who played a combined 26 minutes in the two games prior to Wednesday, might be the last hope of the 2024 draft class.

Dadiet (the 25th pick that year) is out of the rotation and headed toward free agency if, as assumed, the Knicks don’t pick up next season’s contract by Saturday’s deadline. Kevin McCullar Jr. (56th pick) was waived last week. Ariel Hukporti (58th) left for the Sixers in free agency.

A year ago, the main reason the Knicks inked Diawara to a standard contract was his low salary, just to stay under the apron. Then he unexpectedly cracked the rotation. Now Diawara has to wait for the Knicks to settle in comfortably before his next opportunity.

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Brewers have a tough call coming up with superstar catcher William Contreras, who’s a free agent after next season. While he may well join the many past Brewers stars who left midcareer via trade or free agency, how do you replace a multidimensional catcher who’s shown tremendous value throughout Milwaukee’s great October run?

According to sources, the Brewers offered Contreras a three-year deal with a club option for something in the neighborhood of $35M during the 2025 season. The bid was deemed so low Contreras’ side didn’t bother to counter it, and now that the 28-year-old has put together a monster postseason and is also a year closer to free agency, his price surely is skyrocketing.

Contreras is said to be open to remaining with the Brewers but is believed interested in a much longer deal. The catcher contract comps he’s surely looking at are the $140M the Dodgers gave Will Smith for 10 years before he hit free agency and the five-year, $115.5M for J.T. Realmuto. The small-market Brewers rarely hand out nine-figure deals; MVPs Christian Yelich and Ryan Braun are the only exceptions to reach the $100 million mark.

The Brewers more frequently don’t retain their biggest stars long term, with shortstop Willy Adames and pitchers Corbin Burnes and Freddy Peralta prime recent examples. Adames left as a free agent, signing for $181M with the Giants, while the Brewers traded Corbin Burnes to the Orioles for DL Hall and Joey Ortiz, and dealt Freddy Peralta to the Mets for Jett Williams and Brandon Sproat. Burnes wound up signing for $210M over six seasons a year after his trade, and Peralta, now facing Milwaukee in the World Series as a Tampa Bay Ray, appears in line for a contract in the $150M range(link).

news.originalContent:

Supporters of Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed told Fox News Digital the Great Lake State is due for a progressive champion and person of color in statewide office.

“I personally think he’s resonating with people in Michigan because he is a person of color, obviously, and then, secondly, he gets down, and he’s 10 toes down,” said Emily Walker, a teacher at Cass Technical High School, the venue where El-Sayed hosted a rally on Saturday.

“He’s out here with the people. He’s knocking on doors. He’s talking to the community,” Walker added. “He’s also a medical professional, and I just feel like he’s very educated, and he understands what’s going on in policies.”

Fox News Digital spoke with voters outside Cass Technical High School, where El-Sayed hosted a campaign rally featuring former President Barack Obama Saturday.

Obama’s appearance alongside El-Sayed became a major event as the progressive candidate continues working to consolidate backing across the Democratic Party spectrum ahead of the November general election against Republican nominee Mike Rogers.

While exiting the overflow venue, supporters were asked for their thoughts on guaranteed income programs and whether candidates should campaign for them.

“I think we need a major change in what we have with Donald Trump and his cohorts,” said Dave, an attendee at the event. “The Democrats, I don’t think, have been listening well enough. I think we need to change big time instead of just slowly.”

Kiana Montgomery, a publicist attending the rally, agreed that El-Sayed’s message aligns with what local voters are seeking.

“I think he won because he is speaking to the things that are important to people: education, healthcare and bringing down the costs that are going on right now,” Montgomery said. “People are trying to do more than just exist. They’re trying to thrive, and they’re unable to do that in the economic times right now.”

El-Sayed’s campaign platform centers heavily on universal healthcare through Medicare-for-all, raising the federal minimum wage and expanding social safety net initiatives. He has also voiced support for guaranteed income program, government-distributed financial assistance provided without strings attached, to support residents during economic hardship or pregnancy.

Jamal Jenkins told Fox News Digital progressive proposals are finding traction because voters want tangible action on the cost of living.

“I think a progressive is resonating because people want to see more action towards putting a dent into affordability,” Jenkins said. “When you look at corporate profits and the wealth gap between the wealthy, the shrinking middle class and the impoverished, I think folks want to see action. So, more people are actively participating in a positive way in the economy and can live a dignified life.

“I think everybody wants the same thing for themselves and for their kids,” Jenkins added. “Just to have a shot at an education, a good life, work-life balance and to live life without having to struggle as much for reasons that really don’t make much sense.”

El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and former Wayne County health director, has made expanding healthcare coverage a central focus of his bid to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. He has consistently championed Medicare-for-all to create a government-funded health coverage system.

Mohammed, a resident of Bloomfield Hills, said El-Sayed brings fresh perspective to economic and foreign policy discussions.

“The old way of doing business isn’t working anymore,” Mohammed said. “We don’t want to see our money being taken away from us. We want to see our money being used for the children here, for the elderly here and for those in need. With our grocery prices and gas prices being the way they are, we shouldn’t be fighting stupid wars anymore, as he keeps saying.

“I think for all of us as citizens of Michigan, he’s a better fit because he’s looking out for us as opposed to big pharma and PACs.”

El-Sayed has bristled at media questions about his criticism of Israel, which has become a mainstream position in the Democratic Party, saying it distracts from issues voters want to talk about.

El-Sayed and Mike Rogers’ campaigns did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Three alleged noncitizens in Southern California were indicted by a federal grand jury Wednesday on elected fraud charges after a sprawling takedown of suspected illegal voting across California.

The three were identified as Mexican national Sulema De Leon, Cambodian national Butleng Taing and Canadian national Rouzbeh Seyamaknejad — all of whom are accused of illegally registering to vote, according to the Department of Justice.

The indictments follow busts across California last week that snared 28 suspects in what authorities called the state’s biggest-ever voter fraud bust.

De Leon, 35, of Long Beach, is accused of illegally registering to vote in 2013 before casting a ballot in 2020 while falsely denying to have claimed US citizenship, authorities said.

Taing, 43, also of Long Beach, is accused of illegally registering to vote in 2021, voting in 2022 and 2024, and falsely denying prior US citizenship claims.

Seyamaknejad, 63, of Rancho Palos Verdes, is accused of illegally registering to vote in 2018 and falsely denying to have claimed US citizenship.

“The grand jury has started returning indictments against noncitizens who registered to vote, including those who voted in prior elections,” said LA’s top federal prosecutor, Bill Essayli.

“Safeguarding the integrity of our elections remains a top priory for our office and we will continue investigating and charging election fraud.”

The defendants swept up last Monday in “Operation Protect the Vote” were charged in federal courts with a range of crimes, including false statements in naturalization applications.

They were identified from a list of more than 20,000 suspected noncitizens in the state who allegedly registered to vote in next month’s midterm election.

The California Post was there as Homeland Security Investigations swooped in on the City of Commerce home of Omar Alexander Muñoz around 6 a.m., swiftly taking him into custody.

Muñoz, 72, a Belizean national, is accused of fraudulently registering to vote in September 2019, claiming he was a US citizen, according to prosecutors. He then voted in US elections in 2020, twice in 2022 and in 2024, court papers say.

Muñoz also allegedly lied on his application to become a naturalized US citizen, when he falsely stated under oath to have never claimed US citizenship, investigators say. He faces felony charges including making false statements in a naturalization application.

The list of 20,000 suspected noncitizens was front and center in a Los Angeles courtroom on Tuesday, where Bill Essayli demanded ballots believed to be cast by those on the list be segregated.

Essayli pushed for a preliminary injunction, warning that 500,000 ballots have already been counted and any votes cast by noncitizens could be included in the tally.

“We are not seeking to change the rules. As we speak thousands of ballots are being counted. We have a strong interest in election integrity,” Essayli told a packed courtroom.

Los Angeles’ top federal prosecutor has warned upcoming midterm elections are under serious risk of being “corrupted.”

Federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections, and the government says some people have faced criminal charges over alleged illegal registration and voting.

“Every minute that goes by, American citizen votes are being diluted in the state of California,” Essayli said last week.

news.originalContent:
Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc leads but is falling short of the votes needed to form a government.

No clear winner has emerged from Israel’s election, with nearly 90 percent of ballots counted and both major political blocs falling short of the 61 seats needed to form a government.

The Israeli Central Elections Committee said on Wednesday that it had counted more than five million votes as of 9pm local time (19:00 GMT). Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc is on course to win 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot is expected to secure 48 seats.

Projections from Tuesday’s voting also showed that the Arab parties – the Joint List and Ra’am – could hold a record combined 19 seats.

Final election results could come as early as Thursday evening, though no clear winner is expected to emerge.

More than 500,000 special double-envelope ballots remain to be counted, potentially changing the seat distribution. These include votes cast by soldiers, diplomats and others voting away from their registered polling stations.

The vote – the first since the October 7, 2023, attacks and the Gaza genocide – was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s premiership. The 77-year-old appears far from defeated, despite lacking a clear majority.

Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed. President Isaac Herzog will begin consulting party leaders about forming a new administration next week, once the official election results are released.

Herzog has urged all parties to avoid another vote that would stall the formation of a government. But coalition building is the norm in Israel, and no party has ever won an outright majority in the country’s history.

Ahead of the vote, Eisenkot ruled out forming a minority government with Arab-led parties. Netanyahu has also rejected such a prospect.

As Netanyahu’s bloc is set to be the largest, analysts predict that he will form a unity government that could include Eisenkot. However, such an outcome is far from certain.

Eisenkot said in a post on X on Wednesday that his opposition alliance was now focused on the “heavy task entrusted to us – bringing change to Israel and establishing a Zionist mobilisation government”.

“This is the will of the people who expressed no confidence in the government of October 7th and the shirking, and in the bloc of shirkers in general. A bloc that is at the low point of two decades.”

Amid record turnout among Arab voters, Netanyahu’s Likud party accused Arab parties of stealing the election.

“The elections in the State of Israel were stolen by Arab parties that support terrorism and the elimination of the Jewish state through serious criminal offences of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries, and the use of prohibited software to mobilise voters,” the party said in a statement.

“The Likud party is transferring to the police, the Shin Bet, and the Central Elections Committee hundreds of testimonies and pieces of evidence regarding election theft in many Arab polling stations,” it said.

Israel’s predominantly Arab Joint List political alliance said in a statement published late on Wednesday by Turkish news agency Anadolu that preliminary figures showed Arab voter turnout played a decisive role in keeping Netanyahu and his coalition short of a parliamentary majority, while cautioning that the final results were yet to be announced.

Voters answered incitement and intimidation at the ballot box, it said, rejecting a “government of butchers” and its policies of home demolitions, racism and war crimes.

The Joint List said its electoral support reflected demands for political unity and a force capable of defending Arab citizens’ rights without concessions.

It pledged to work to remove Netanyahu’s government and prevent its return, saying it was ready to cooperate towards an alternative government.

Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said the alliance could back an anti-Netanyahu government from outside, but would not join it.

news.originalContent:
The Bucharest court has extended the pre-trial detention of Calin Georgescu by 30 days, appealing a lower court ruling.

A Romanian court has extended the pre-trial detention of far-right politician Calin Georgescu by 30 days, in an investigation into an alleged 1.1 million euros ($1.2m) fraud case.

The decision by the Bucharest Court of Appeal overturned an October 13 ruling by a lower court that ordered the pro-Russian former frontrunner in Romania’s cancelled 2024 presidential election to be moved from police custody to house arrest for 30 days pending the fraud probe.

Prosecutors said Georgescu and two other suspects persuaded a Romanian businessman to give them 1.1 million euros by making him believe they could help him secure a credit line of up to 15 million euros ($16.7m) from a foreign financial institution.

Georgescu denied any wrongdoing and claimed the investigations were “politically motivated”.

Hundreds of Georgescu supporters protested against his investigation, with groups entering the Bucharest court building on Wednesday to demand his release, according to media reports.

George Simion, leader of the hard-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians, said the initial lower court ruling was a sign protesters were being heard.

Following Wednesday’s appeal decision, Georgescu remained in police custody with his detention set until November 27.

The former candidate won the most votes in the first round of Romania’s presidential election in November 2024.

The results and the second round were scrapped following allegations of Russian interference, though Moscow denied interfering in the vote.

Georgescu was subsequently barred from standing again, and pro-European centrist Nicusor Dan ultimately won the rerun presidential election in May 2025.

In a separate case, prosecutors accused Georgescu of instigating violence after the ballot was annulled, disseminating false information, attempting to disrupt national security and promoting 1930s fascist leaders.

Other far-right politicians supported Georgescu and vowed to stand by him amid ongoing political uncertainty in the country.

Parliament approved a government proposed by pro-European Luca Niculescu this month, making him prime minister following months of deadlock after the previous coalition collapsed in May.

news.originalContent:
UN experts have condemned police crackdowns, warning they deter demonstrators from exercising their rights.

United Nations experts have expressed alarm at the “excessive use of force” by French authorities in dispersing the recent nationwide student protests.

“The scale of the arrests and detention, affecting several thousand people, mainly minors, appears disproportionate and deters demonstrators from exercising their freedoms of expression and peaceful assembly,” the four experts, mandated by the UN Human Rights Council, said in a statement on Wednesday.

They included Gina Romero, special rapporteur on the freedom of peaceful assembly, and Farida Shaheed, the UN expert on cultural rights.

“Although authorities launched several initiatives to facilitate dialogue and respond to students’ demands in October, the priority given to a primarily security-focused response to the protests has led to the root causes of the mobilisation being sidelined,” the statement said.

France has seen ongoing student protests since mid-September, sparked initially over conditions in high schools, where young people complained about the deteriorating buildings, overcrowded classrooms and teacher absences. Students have also joined nationwide demonstrations to express anger over the rising cost of living, which led to riots and looting on the sidelines.

The French government deployed 70,000 security forces and arrested 1,000 people during demonstrations on Saturday, which drew 410,000 protesters nationwide, France’s Interior Ministry said. A week earlier, public buildings were vandalised, hundreds of businesses were looted and 2,700 people were arrested, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez vowing to be “extremely vigilant, extremely firm” to quell future unrest.

“What we are seeing right now is a general outburst of resentment against [French President Emmanuel] Macron and his policies that have destroyed our rights, destroyed our living conditions,” Alice Cohen-Morzadec, a spokesperson for the Union Etudiante, told Al Jazeera.

Analysts say the French government has struggled to address students’ demands due to a severe fiscal crisis and planned budget cuts, which have led to a drop in the country’s education budget.

French authorities have been criticised for their approach to security during some of the protests, and in one case a teenager in the northern city of Lille lost a hand when a grenade exploded as school protesters clashed with police.

“The serious and, in some cases, irreversible injuries sustained by underage demonstrators during law enforcement operations are unacceptable and unjustifiable,” the UN rapporteurs said.

The statement added: “The experts recalled past discussions urging French authorities to undertake a comprehensive review of their policing strategies and practices in order to enable demonstrators to express their concerns and to facilitate a peaceful resolution of social conflicts.”

“The experts are in contact with French authorities on the issue,” the statement concluded.

news.originalContent:
President Laura Fernandez inaugurated the $35m mega-prison built to house up to 5,100 inmates near San Jose.

A newly opened maximum-security mega-prison in Costa Rica has received its first batch of inmates. The prison was built with the help of the Salvadoran government on the outskirts of the capital, San Jose, the country’s Justice Ministry announced.

The Costa Rican Justice Ministry shared images on Tuesday of 123 inmates dressed in orange, seated with their heads shaved and bowed and their hands behind their necks.

“Costa Rica is writing a new chapter in its penitentiary history,” Justice Minister Gabriel Aguilar said in a statement.

The new prison is called the High-Containment Center Against Organized Crime (CACCO) and constitutes a symbol of a new “tough on crime” approach championed by President Laura Fernandez’s administration. It has a capacity for 5,100 inmates.

The CACCO was built with the help of the Salvadoran government on the outskirts of Costa Rica’s capital, San Jose, at a cost of $35m. Fernandez inaugurated it on October 15.

“CACCO is a monument to national security, a forceful response to organized crime, and a guarantee that the state will exercise its authority without hesitation,” the statement added.

The new facility has a capacity equivalent to 20 percent of the country’s prison population and “will also help reduce overcrowding in the prison system”, according to Aguilar.

Costa Rica, long regarded as one of the safest countries in Latin America, has in recent years experienced a sharp rise in violence linked to drug trafficking and organised crime. It witnessed a record-setting 905 homicides in 2023, followed by 876 in 2024 and 873 in 2025.

Authorities attribute most killings to disputes between criminal groups over drug trafficking routes and markets.

Right-wing leaders in other Latin American countries have also sought to replicate the mega-prison model.

news.title: وزیر کشور صربستان: یک مهاجم که با خود چاقو داشت، پس از حمله به پلیس در مقابل سفارت اسرائیل کشته شد
news.originalSummary:
منبع تصویر، Andrej ISAKOVIC / AFP via Getty Images

پلیس صربستان گفته است که بامداد امروز پس از وقوع یک «حمله تروریستی»، نیروهای این کشور مرد جوانی را در مقابل سفارت اسرائیل به ضرب گلوله کشتند.

ایویتسا داچیچ، وزیر کشور صربستان، گفت مهاجم در حالی که دو چاقو در دست داشت با فریاد «الله‌اکبر» به یک مأمور پلیس حمله‌ور شد. این مامور که از ناحیه صورت جراحتی سطحی برداشت، مهاجم را هدف گلوله قرار داد.

آقای داچیچ گفت او نوجوانی تبعه صربستان بود که سرویس‌های امنیتی او را زیر نظر داشتند، زیرا «به‌عنوان حامی گروه دولت اسلامی شناخته می‌شد». جزئیات بیشتری از هویت این فرد منتشر نشده است.

وزیر کشور صربستان در گفت‌وگو با خبرنگاران در مقابل سفارت گفت تحقیقات ادامه دارد، اما سرویس‌های امنیتی اعلام کرده‌اند که مظنون تصویری از پرچم گروه موسوم به دولت اسلامی (داعش) را در صفحه اینستاگرام خود منتشر کرده بود.

آقای داچیچ سطح تهدید تروریستی در صربستان را به «وضعیت قرمز» ارتقا داد که بالاترین سطح هشدار است. این اقدام به معنای تشدید بازرسی‌های امنیتی و افزایش حضور پلیس در مکان‌هایی مانند تاسیسات زیربنایی و محل‌های تجمع جمعیت‌های بزرگ است.

وزیر کشور صربستان گفت به دیدار پلیس مجروح رفته است. گزارش شده که حال این مأمور خوب است و جراحاتش به بستری شدن در بیمارستان نیاز نداشته است.

صبح چهارشنبه نیروهای امنیتی مسلح در حال نگهبانی در مقابل سفارت اسرائیل دیده شدند.

وزارت خارجه اسرائیل در پیامی در شبکه‌های اجتماعی تأیید کرد که هیچ‌یک از کارکنان سفارت آسیب ندیده‌اند و این نمایندگی دیپلماتیک هنگام وقوع حادثه تعطیل بوده است.

این دومین حمله از این نوع به سفارت اسرائیل در بلگراد طی کمتر از سه سال است. در ژوئن ۲۰۲۴، مردی با تیرکمان به گردن یک مأمور پلیس تیر پرتاب کرده بود.

آن مأمور از حمله جان سالم به در برد و مهاجم را کشت. مهاجم مردی صرب بود که به اسلام گرویده بود.

news.originalContent:
با ادامه شمارش آرا در انتخابات عمومی اسرائیل، به نظر می‌رسد بنیامین نتانیاهو بهتر از آنچه عموما پیش‌بینی شده بود، عمل کرده است.

در حالی که طبق نتایج اولیه انتخابات اسرائیل، هیچیک از دو نامزد اصلی یعنی بنیامین نتانیاهو و گادی آیزنکوت به اکثریت لازم برای به دست گرفتن پارلمان نرسیده‌اند، هر دو می‌گویند که برای تشکیل دولت تلاش خواهند کرد.

کمی پیش‌تر، نظرسنجی‌های پس از رأی‌گیری نشان می‌داد که اردوگاه بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست‌وزیر، و اردوگاه رقیب او شانه‌به‌شانه یکدیگر پیش می‌روند.

تا این لحظه هیچ یک از این دو جناح ۶۱ کرسی مورد نیاز برای تشکیل دولت را به دست نیاورده‌اند.

این در حالی است که فهرست‌های انتخاباتی اعراب اسرائیل، عملکردی قوی داشتند و بر اساس نظرسنجی‌ها، مجموعاً ۱۷ یا ۱۸ کرسی را از آن خود خواهند کرد.

در اینجا چهار سناریوی احتمالی مطرح است:

احزاب بلافاصله مذاکرات خود را برای دستیابی به اکثریت ۶۱ کرسی آغاز خواهند کرد، اما مسیر پیش رو به‌هیچ‌وجه روشن نیست.

اسحاق هرتزوگ، رئیس‌جمهور اسرائيل، نامزدی را مأمور تشکیل دولت خواهد کرد که بیشترین شانس را برای این کار داشته باشد اما این فرد لزوماً از حزبی که بیشترین کرسی‌ها را کسب کرده، نخواهد بود.

احزاب عرب اسرائیل، به‌ویژه حزب رعام یا «حزب متحد عربی»، برای همکاری با جناح آقای آیزنکوت ابراز آمادگی کرده‌اند اما این جناح از آن‌ها فاصله گرفته و حمایتشان را در طول کارزار انتخاباتی، نوعی نقطه ضعف تلقی کرده است.

در مقابل، برای جناح آقای نتانیاهو نیز راه مشخصی برای کسب کرسی‌های بیشتر وجود ندارد، به‌ویژه پس از آنکه برخی احزاب راست‌گرای کوچکتر نتوانستند حد نصاب لازم برای ورود به پارلمان را به دست آورند.

مذاکرات ائتلافی می‌تواند بسیار دشوار و فرساینده باشد، چرا که احزاب بر منافع خاص و محدود خود پافشاری می‌کنند؛ چنین روندی ممکن است به تشکیل دولت‌هایی ناپایدار منجر شود.

پس از انتخابات پیشین در نوامبر ۲۰۲۲، تشکیل دولت جدید آقای نتانیاهو ۵۸ روز طول کشید.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اگر هیچ‌یک از جناح‌ها موفق به کسب ۶۱ کرسی نشوند، ممکن است نامزدی تلاش کند بدون داشتن اکثریت، دولت تشکیل دهد و در عوض، برای پیشبرد امور، به حمایت‌های موردی و مقطعی سایر قانون‌گذاران متکی باشد.

در این سناریو، نمایندگان احزاب عرب اسرائیل که ۲۰ درصد از جمعیت کشور را تشکیل می‌دهند، می‌توانند نقشی حیاتی ایفا کنند.

حزب رعام یا حزب متحد عربی به رهبری منصور عباس، پیش‌تر نقش تعیین‌کننده‌ای ایفا کرده؛ چرا که نخستین حزب عربی بود که در ائتلافی کوتاه‌مدت (۲۰۲۱-۲۰۲۲) به رهبری نفتالی بنت و یائیر لاپید، به دولت اسرائیل پیوست.

یک جریان عربی دیگر به نام «فهرست مشترک» اعلام کرده که بعید است مستقیماً به یک دولت ائتلافی بپیوندد، اما پیشنهاد داده که برای هر کسی که حزب آقای نتانیاهو را از قدرت کنار بزند، نقش یک حامی را ایفا کند.

تال الویتز، تحلیلگر سیاسی، می‌گوید که مشارکت به‌ویژه بالای اعراب در انتخابات، «نشان‌دهنده تمایلی قوی برای مشارکت [در قدرت] است».

گادی آیزنکوت حتی به‌طور علنی چنین احتمالی را مطرح نکرده در حالی که بنیامین نتانیاهو در کارزار انتخاباتی خود پیوسته به رأی‌دهندگان یهودی هشدار می‌داد که رأی دادن به جناح مخالف ممکن است منجر به ورود اعراب به دولت شود.

آقای الویتز می‌گوید: «در حال حاضر، به نظر می‌رسد احتمال تشکیل یک دولت اقلیت به رهبری گادی آیزنکوت وجود دارد، اما بسته به نتایج نهایی، این وضعیت همچنان ممکن است تغییر کند.»

با توجه به دوقطبی‌شدن فضای سیاسی در اسرائیل، چشم‌انداز تشکیل یک «دولت وحدت ملی» دور از ذهن به نظر می‌رسد، اما از نظر تئوریک می‌تواند منجر به تشکیل دولتی شود که مواضع افراطی کمتری دارد.

تحلیلگران اسرائیلی بارها درباره احتمال تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی گمانه‌زنی کرده‌اند؛ دولتی که در آن آقای نتانیاهو متحدان راست‌گرای افراطی خود، و همچنین احزاب یهودیان ارتدوکس راست‌گرا را کنار بگذارد و با آقای آیزنکوت همراه شود که در بسیاری از مسائل امنیتی، دیدگاه‌هایی همسو با آقای نتانیاهو دارد.

چنین ائتلاف بزرگی، احزاب عربی را نیز شامل نخواهد شد.

بر اساس یک نظرسنجی که در ۱۶ اکتبر منتشر شد، اگر انتخابات منجر به کسب اکثریت قاطع از سوی هیچ‌یک از طرفین نشود، ۵۵ درصد از اسرائیلی‌ها تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی را به برگزاری انتخابات جدید ترجیح می‌دهند.

این سناریو یک نمونه مشابه در گذشته نه چندان دور دارد.

در سال ۲۰۲۰، بنیامین نتانیاهو و بنی گانتس، که او نیز مانند گادی آیزنکوت یک ژنرال بازنشسته است و به جریان میانه گرایش دارد، پس از سه دوره انتخابات در کمتر از یک سال، به توافقی برای تقسیم قدرت دست یافتند.

این توافق شامل چرخش مقام نخست‌وزیری بود، اما این شراکت پس از یک سال از هم پاشید و منجر به برگزاری انتخاباتی دیگر شد.

تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی در شرایط کنونی با مخالفت شدید هر دو طرف، به‌ویژه جناح مخالف حزب حاکم مواجه خواهد شد؛ جناحی که محور کارزار انتخاباتی خود را، کنار زدن آقای نتانیاهو و معرفی او به‌عنوان فردی فاقد صلاحیت برای رهبری، قرار داده است.

اگر هیچ‌یک از نامزدها موفق به تشکیل دولت نشوند، مردم اسرائیل ناچار خواهند بود بار دیگر به پای صندوق‌های رأی بروند.

این کشور بین آوریل ۲۰۱۹ تا مارس ۲۰۲۱، به دلیل ناتوانی سیاستمداران در ایجاد یک ائتلاف پایدار، چهار بار انتخابات برگزار کرد.

نامزدی که از سوی رئیس‌جمهور مأمور تشکیل کابینه می‌شود، به‌طور معمول ۲۸ روز فرصت دارد تا ائتلافی تشکیل دهد.

این مهلت می‌تواند ۱۴ روز دیگر نیز تمدید شود.

البته راهکارهای آیین‌نامه‌ای دیگری نیز وجود دارد که می‌توان از طریق آن‌ها از برگزاری فوری انتخابات جدید جلوگیری کرد.

احزاب عرب اسرائیل، به‌ویژه حزب رعام یا «حزب متحد عربی»، برای همکاری با جناح آقای آیزنکوت ابراز آمادگی کرده‌اند اما این جناح از آن‌ها فاصله گرفته و حمایتشان را در طول کارزار انتخاباتی، نوعی نقطه ضعف تلقی کرده است.

در مقابل، برای جناح آقای نتانیاهو نیز راه مشخصی برای کسب کرسی‌های بیشتر وجود ندارد، به‌ویژه پس از آنکه برخی احزاب راست‌گرای کوچکتر نتوانستند حد نصاب لازم برای ورود به پارلمان را به دست آورند.

مذاکرات ائتلافی می‌تواند بسیار دشوار و فرساینده باشد، چرا که احزاب بر منافع خاص و محدود خود پافشاری می‌کنند؛ چنین روندی ممکن است به تشکیل دولت‌هایی ناپایدار منجر شود.

پس از انتخابات پیشین در نوامبر ۲۰۲۲، تشکیل دولت جدید آقای نتانیاهو ۵۸ روز طول کشید.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

اگر هیچ‌یک از جناح‌ها موفق به کسب ۶۱ کرسی نشوند، ممکن است نامزدی تلاش کند بدون داشتن اکثریت، دولت تشکیل دهد و در عوض، برای پیشبرد امور، به حمایت‌های موردی و مقطعی سایر قانون‌گذاران متکی باشد.

در این سناریو، نمایندگان احزاب عرب اسرائیل که ۲۰ درصد از جمعیت کشور را تشکیل می‌دهند، می‌توانند نقشی حیاتی ایفا کنند.

حزب رعام یا حزب متحد عربی به رهبری منصور عباس، پیش‌تر نقش تعیین‌کننده‌ای ایفا کرده؛ چرا که نخستین حزب عربی بود که در ائتلافی کوتاه‌مدت (۲۰۲۱-۲۰۲۲) به رهبری نفتالی بنت و یائیر لاپید، به دولت اسرائیل پیوست.

یک جریان عربی دیگر به نام «فهرست مشترک» اعلام کرده که بعید است مستقیماً به یک دولت ائتلافی بپیوندد، اما پیشنهاد داده که برای هر کسی که حزب آقای نتانیاهو را از قدرت کنار بزند، نقش یک حامی را ایفا کند.

تال الویتز، تحلیلگر سیاسی، می‌گوید که مشارکت به‌ویژه بالای اعراب در انتخابات، «نشان‌دهنده تمایلی قوی برای مشارکت [در قدرت] است».

گادی آیزنکوت حتی به‌طور علنی چنین احتمالی را مطرح نکرده در حالی که بنیامین نتانیاهو در کارزار انتخاباتی خود پیوسته به رأی‌دهندگان یهودی هشدار می‌داد که رأی دادن به جناح مخالف ممکن است منجر به ورود اعراب به دولت شود.

آقای الویتز می‌گوید: «در حال حاضر، به نظر می‌رسد احتمال تشکیل یک دولت اقلیت به رهبری گادی آیزنکوت وجود دارد، اما بسته به نتایج نهایی، این وضعیت همچنان ممکن است تغییر کند.»

با توجه به دوقطبی‌شدن فضای سیاسی در اسرائیل، چشم‌انداز تشکیل یک «دولت وحدت ملی» دور از ذهن به نظر می‌رسد، اما از نظر تئوریک می‌تواند منجر به تشکیل دولتی شود که مواضع افراطی کمتری دارد.

تحلیلگران اسرائیلی بارها درباره احتمال تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی گمانه‌زنی کرده‌اند؛ دولتی که در آن آقای نتانیاهو متحدان راست‌گرای افراطی خود، و همچنین احزاب یهودیان ارتدوکس راست‌گرا را کنار بگذارد و با آقای آیزنکوت همراه شود که در بسیاری از مسائل امنیتی، دیدگاه‌هایی همسو با آقای نتانیاهو دارد.

چنین ائتلاف بزرگی، احزاب عربی را نیز شامل نخواهد شد.

بر اساس یک نظرسنجی که در ۱۶ اکتبر منتشر شد، اگر انتخابات منجر به کسب اکثریت قاطع از سوی هیچ‌یک از طرفین نشود، ۵۵ درصد از اسرائیلی‌ها تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی را به برگزاری انتخابات جدید ترجیح می‌دهند.

این سناریو یک نمونه مشابه در گذشته نه چندان دور دارد.

در سال ۲۰۲۰، بنیامین نتانیاهو و بنی گانتس، که او نیز مانند گادی آیزنکوت یک ژنرال بازنشسته است و به جریان میانه گرایش دارد، پس از سه دوره انتخابات در کمتر از یک سال، به توافقی برای تقسیم قدرت دست یافتند.

این توافق شامل چرخش مقام نخست‌وزیری بود، اما این شراکت پس از یک سال از هم پاشید و منجر به برگزاری انتخاباتی دیگر شد.

تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی در شرایط کنونی با مخالفت شدید هر دو طرف، به‌ویژه جناح مخالف حزب حاکم مواجه خواهد شد؛ جناحی که محور کارزار انتخاباتی خود را، کنار زدن آقای نتانیاهو و معرفی او به‌عنوان فردی فاقد صلاحیت برای رهبری، قرار داده است.

اگر هیچ‌یک از نامزدها موفق به تشکیل دولت نشوند، مردم اسرائیل ناچار خواهند بود بار دیگر به پای صندوق‌های رأی بروند.

این کشور بین آوریل ۲۰۱۹ تا مارس ۲۰۲۱، به دلیل ناتوانی سیاستمداران در ایجاد یک ائتلاف پایدار، چهار بار انتخابات برگزار کرد.

نامزدی که از سوی رئیس‌جمهور مأمور تشکیل کابینه می‌شود، به‌طور معمول ۲۸ روز فرصت دارد تا ائتلافی تشکیل دهد.

این مهلت می‌تواند ۱۴ روز دیگر نیز تمدید شود.

البته راهکارهای آیین‌نامه‌ای دیگری نیز وجود دارد که می‌توان از طریق آن‌ها از برگزاری فوری انتخابات جدید جلوگیری کرد.

After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto [GTA] VI is set to arrive next month and over a million Americans are forecast to call out sick when it drops.

Economists are actually predicting this could cause America’s GDP to take a $1 billion hit on its release day, according to International Business Times.

I hate to sound the alarm but the effect this game will have is being severely underestimated. GTA VI has been so hyped at this point that it’s expected to be nothing less than a digital fentanyl black hole, and, according to my calculations, gamers will cross its event horizon and never return to work.

Don’t go outside either — DoorDash drivers will be driving recklessly to deliver pizza to couch-locked gamers.

Even accounting for GDP gain from delivery drivers working overtime, we are still looking at a 2008-style crash times a million.

President Trump: Fortify GameStops and order a shelter-in-place on Nov. 19. For safety purposes, obviously.

2. Hotties in SF: An Invasive Species?

Wednesday, Pirate Wires reported that SF, once a wasteland for uggos, is now teeming with beautiful women.

On X, these women post viral selfies announcing their new jobs in AI sales and growth, while men we interviewed are clocking 10s in the Marina.

Is this a sign we’re in … a bubble? AI startups, swimming in VC cash, are now shifting their energies toward buying attention, i.e., sexy saleswomen to help them stand out.

Whether those eyeballs convert to customers is questionable, but as the debate continues over whether baddies in the Bay means the economy is about to tank, consider these examples of peak froth: One AI company hired a “Head of Coffee” (whaaaat?), another offers Porches to employees who refer new engineers, and a third pays staff $1,000 monthly to live nearby.

Enjoy the blondes, booze and cars while they last, friends (and maybe consider shorting the market).

3. Uhhh I think it’s about the Antichrist?

You may have heard about Peter Thiel’s Antichrist lectures. For months, journalists have speculated about Thiel’s motivation.

Was he, given the lectures’ anti-regulation theme, merely talking his book? Or, my personal favorite: Was he trying to come off as a “zany contrarian” to help raise money? (As though Thiel needs help with either of those things.)

Courtesy of G.B. Rango’s new 10,000-word essay (the first to seriously engage with the actual content of the lectures), we’re offering our own take: Peter Thiel actually cares a great deal about the Antichrist!

The lectures are dense, academic works of political theology. They posit that the Antichrist is a modern threat because of strengthening infrastructure for worldwide tyranny, among other factors.

Like, sorry, but this is just the feverish work of a zany, neurodivergent, intellectual contrarian. You should read GB’s piece, if you want to try to follow along, and maybe the Bible while you’re at it.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The four kids allegedly left by their photographer mom during her Las Vegas trip were left unsupervised for about 16 hours per day – while their babysitter lived two hours, Florida cops revealed Wednesday.

Irene Miller, 50, is facing four counts of child endangerment – and a combined maximum sentence of 20 years behind bars – after Osceola County authorities say she left her children, 9, 11, 12 and 14 alone at their Kissimmee condo while traveling to Sin City on a five-day work trip starting Oct. 18.

Outside of school hours, the children’s only adult contact came from a babysitter hired by Miller who arrived at 8 a.m. to drop them off  at school and left at 4 p.m. after they were home, Capt. Kim Montes from the Osceola Sheriff’s Office told The Post.

The caretaker also was not nearby in case of an emergency, she lives two hours away near Tampa, according to authorities.

Cops found that while the condo was well maintained and not messy, there was relatively little food in the fridge for the kids, Montes said.

The alleged neglect was eventually uncovered after the 11-year-old girl and 12-year-old boy called 911 in a panic over their youngest sibling getting struck in the head by a dumbbell that came crashing down while he was building a fort at around 8:30 p.m. on Oct. 21.

“He was building a fort with sheets and blankets and he used the dumbbell to secure a sheet on a piece of furniture, but when he pulled the sheet, it fell and hit him on his forehead,” said Montes, adding that the laceration was later glued back together at the hospital.

The eldest sibling, who was outside riding his bike during the accident, only learned what had happened when first responders showed up at the house and began asking questions.

“When we got there, the 14-year-old shows back up because he sees all the fire trucks, and we ask where the mom is. They said she’s out of town,” Montes recalled.

Deputies soon reached Miller on her cell phone, however, she was “very dismissive to the deputy, saying that she’s working right now.

“Then, [she] says she is going to have to go and hangs up on the deputy,” Montes said.

The captain was even more shocked at what happened next.

Miller “proceeds to call the 14-year-old on his cell phone, and I don’t want to use the word yell…but basically tells the 14-year-old, ‘Why are you calling 911? You’re going to get me in trouble,’” she said.

“She’s berating the son for calling 911…while he was standing right there with the deputy. It was on speaker.”

“So she knew what she did was wrong,” Montes said, then noted a concerning observation made by cops.

“The house was clean, the kids were clean. The deputy did notice that there wasn’t a lot of food there…There just didn’t seem to be a lot of food there for four children.”

Still, Miller didn’t turn around and fly home – even as her son was hospitalized, cops said.

Later that night, all four of the kids were placed in the care of her husband, who was arrested in August for alleged spousal abuse.

Mark Miller, 53, was hit with a criminal battery charge and restraining order after his wife of 15 years accused him of slapping her phone out of her hand during a heated confrontation outside of their kids’ school, according to court documents reviewed by The Post.

He has pleaded not guilty to the charge.

Irene Miller, who was born in Russia, then filed a petition for a dissolution of marriage against Mark Miller, who was born in Ukraine, just last month, the docs show.

“The kids were ecstatic to see [their father]…like hugging him, happy to go with him, very ecstatic to see him,” Montes said, adding that the court-ordered no contact order between the parents did not mean the kids could not stay with their dad.

Mark Miller and the children have reportedly been staying at a motel since then.

Irene Miller was met by cops at the Orlando Airport upon her return from Las Vegas on Friday of last week – a day and a half after the accident.

She was arrested and booked into Orange County Jail, but posted her $4,000 surety bond on Saturday.

Her next court date wasn’t immediately clear.

A popular San Luis Obispo pumpkin patch has been linked to an outbreak of E. coli that has sickened several people — leaving three children in the intensive care unit.

The San Luis Obispo County Department of Public Health said it had confirmed five cases of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli linked to the Brookshire Farms pumpkin patch.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

“We have five people who are infected with a type of E. Coli that can cause bloody diarrhea and vomiting and then in young children cause renal disease and sometimes kidney failure,” County Health Officer Christy Mulkerin told KSBY.

Three of infected are children in serious condition at the pediatric ICU, the health department said.

While the source still needs to be confirmed, officials said all of those infected visited the pumpkin patch.

“We know that there’s a link that these people all went to Brookshire Farms but we’re still investigating exactly how they could’ve gotten sick,” Mulkerin said.

“We are working diligently to identify the source of these infections to protect the health of our community.”

Officials described the exposure period as between October 16 and 26.

On Tuesday, the farm closed its doors voluntarily. The health department said it would remain closed until testing is complete. Results are expected to take several days.

Brookshire’s owner said the farm is fully cooperating with authorities.

Officials said anyone who visited the farm between Oct. 16-26 and is experiencing “gastrointestinal symptoms, usually cramping abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea,” typically 3–10 days after they were there, should contact their healthcare provider, noting children have a high risk of developing complications.

“We encourage anyone who may have been exposed and is experiencing symptoms consistent with E. coli infection to seek immediate medical attention,” Mulkerin said.

“Anyone experiencing bloody diarrhea, severe abdominal pain, signs of dehydration or other concerning symptoms should seek medical attention,” officials added.

The health department said the investigation remains ongoing. The California Post reached out to the agency for further comment.

A popular San Luis Obispo pumpkin patch has been linked to an outbreak of E. coli that has sickened several people — leaving three children in the intensive care unit.

The San Luis Obispo County Department of Public Health said it had confirmed five cases of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli linked to the Brookshire Farms pumpkin patch.

“We have five people who are infected with a type of E. Coli that can cause bloody diarrhea and vomiting and then in young children cause renal disease and sometimes kidney failure,” County Health Officer Christy Mulkerin told KSBY.

Three of infected are children in serious condition at the pediatric ICU, the health department said.

While the source still needs to be confirmed, officials said all of those infected visited the pumpkin patch.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

They want to seize the means of party production.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s campaign guru admitted the DSA’s ultimate goal is to “take over” the Democratic Party — by running lefty darling Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for president.

Andrew Epstein, 38, recently told a Belgian newspaper that the Democratic Socialists of America want to build on victories from over the last year, such as Mamdani’s election and comrades Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez soon-to-be joining AOC in Congress.

“I think we want to take over the Democratic Party,” he told Dutch-language outlet De Tijd, according to a translation of the Tuesday article.

To achieve its aim, the DSA needs to run one of their own for president, with the clear choice being AOC, the far-left political strategist said.

“I cannot imagine any other politician who can mobilize the electorate needed to win the presidency,” Epstein was quoted as saying.

“You can only change a party by putting forward a president,” he said, adding, “Just look at how [President] Trump has transformed the Republicans.”

Epstein was the spokesperson and creative mind behind Mamdani’s Democratic mayoral primary campaign that saw the little-known state lawmaker trounce ex-Gov. Andrew Cuomo in a stunning upset that made global headlines.

During the general election that followed, Epstein was moved out of the spotlight during the general election and replaced as campaign spokesperson.

But he continues to have the ear of Mamdani, one of the most influential DSA members in the country.

More recently, Epstein worked on Valdez’s winning campaign in the June Democratic primary for New York’s Seventh House District representing western Queens and north Brooklyn.

Both Valdez and fellow NYC-DSA-er Avila Chevalier were endorsed by Mamdani and are all-but-sure to cruise to victory on November 3 in their overwhelmingly Democratic congressional districts.

The extreme left-wing is looking to score a handful more wins in congressional races next week — with Chris Rabb running in Pennsylvania and Mai Yang and Angela Gonzales-Torres in California.

The DSA is also is also attempting to add to its elected ranks at various levels of state government around the country while riding a socialist wave that many credit to the Big Apple mayor.

Local DSA chapters have endorsed Los Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman and Washington DC mayoral hopeful Janeese Lewis George.

Beyond the midterms, the NYC-DSA have publicly voiced support for a potential Ocasio-Cortez presidential run in 2028.

AOC has been toying with the idea, recently popping around New York state to campaign with local Democrats — though she has not formally announced any potential plans.

Her potential bid has the Democratic establishment — and even some on the left — scrambling.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom, another frontrunner for the party’s nod in 2028, recently warned that the DSA would be an influential force in the next presidential race.

“The DSA, the energy and the desire for bold change, not incremental change, is very much going to be the dominant… I mean that is going to be the mainstream Democratic movement. Absolutely. No question in my mind,” Newsom said.

Epstein told De Tijd he believes the political pendulum has swung in favor of the far-left, with a large swath of millennial voters feeling the “failure of capitalism” after the 2008 financial crash and no longer see the “problems” created by socialism, or even communism.

“The association with socialism is no longer a problem, so they now use the word ‘communist,’” he claimed to the outlet about attacks launched by critics.

“The further we are from the Cold War, the more that anti-socialist culture disappears. Voters want something new now.”

A recent New York Times/Siena poll found that 51% of American voters held an unfavorable view of socialism.

Epstein told The Post that his remarks only represented his own opinions, not those of the DSA.

Nobody circles the wagons quite like the leaders of the global left, who will eagerly line up behind just about anyone — the corrupt, the vindictive, the incompetent and even the openly evil — so long as they perceive them to be “part of the team.”

Take their celebration of the disturbing, real-time collapse of Brazilian democracy for an example.

Incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s triumph over Flávio Bolsonaro in this week’s presidential election occurred under suspicious circumstances.

Lula’s narrow victory came only after Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin — who served as Lula’s personal defense attorney in the criminal case that sent Lula to jail a decade ago before being appointed to his current position by his former client — issued what four electoral lawyers who spoke to The New York Times called an “unprecedented” ruling to extend voting deadlines.

In cities where Bolsonaro was favored, like Rio De Janeiro and Brasilia, the polls closed only shortly after they were originally supposed to.

In Lula’s strongholds of São Paulo and Salvador, they stayed open for the entire two-hour extension.

But nothing — not these shenanigans, nor Lula’s unconstitutional, pre-election bribes; not his tanking of the Brazilian economy, nor his fellowship with dictators across the region and world — dissuaded his shameless sympathizers from popping champagne after his victory.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani declared that “The people united will never be defeated!”

Spanish socialist Pedro Sánchez suggested Lula’s “great victory” heralded “the comeback of global progressivism.”

Alex Soros, heir to George Soros’ destructive left-wing political empire, congratulated Brazilians “for standing up against authoritarianism once again!”

Sen. Bernie Sanders praised Lula for protecting “workers & democracy,” insisting he’d “continue to do so in the next four years.”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen opined that “democracy and multilateralism” had won.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham called it “a true victory for democracy and progressive values.”

And Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a Democratic presidential front-runner, was downright romantic about it all.

“Brazil showed the world that the will of the people is stronger than the authoritarians who try to suppress it,” she swooned.

Already, their applause has aged like milk in the sun.

Within minutes of the announcement of Lula’s “victory,” such as it was, Justice Alexandre de Moraes, another Lula ally on Brazil’s Supreme Court, ordered the seizure of Bolsonaro’s passports in connection with a criminal investigation.

Forget being a sore or ungraceful winner: Lula has gone full banana republic authoritarian.

The opposition leader successfully fled his home for the United States via Argentina, and the details of his escape might make for a fine movie down the line.

In the meantime, though, the state of affairs on the ground is grim.

An incumbent who was convicted on corruption charges before eventually being let off on a technicality just secured a fourth term by unscrupulous means before immediately dispatching a lackey to punish his opponent.

That’s not a blip on the radar, it’s End Times, game over, pack it up, Brazil-is-now-a-democracy-in-name-only stuff.

And the left is doubling down on their celebration of it.

House Democrats aren’t apoplectic over Lula’s power grab; they’re hysterical over the United States’ role in granting Bolsonaro a safe haven.

“Losing an election is not grounds for asylum. Yet the Trump Administration is giving Flávio Bolsonaro safe haven in the United States,” complained Texas’ Joaquin Castro.

“After losing an election, rather than face his pending fraud and corruption charges, Bolsonaro is fleeing Brazil,” tweeted Michigan’s Shri Thanedar. “Congrats to Brazil, democracy always comes out on top!”

Mehdi Hasan, the Islamist-adjacent MSNBC alum who once likened non-Muslims to animals and gays to pedophiles, took things a step further still, fantasizing over the extradition of Mark Zuckerberg to stand trial in one of Lula’s kangaroo courts.

Their affection for the would-be Latin American dictator and envious beholding of his persecution of his enemies is at once alarming and entirely unsurprising.

Because while they’re eager to proclaim their allegiance to small-L liberalism and democracy, their only true allegiance has always been to their own ambition.

It’s why they universally celebrated Alvin Bragg and Letitia James’ cynical lawfare against Donald Trump.

It’s why Sanders honeymooned in the Soviet Union and never met a left-wing strongman he didn’t love.

It’s why Justin Trudeau mourned Fidel Castro’s passing with a love letter that ought to make Katy Perry jealous.

It’s why Hasan has served as a mouthpiece for a slave state.

It’s why Abdul El-Sayed cheered the Muslim Brotherhood’s crackdown on its enemies in 2012.

And it’s why so many poured into the streets to celebrate the Oct. 7 pogrom in 2023.

For these power-hungry jackals, there is no norm they wouldn’t break, no amount of suffering they wouldn’t tolerate, and no authoritarian they wouldn’t embrace if it served their purposes.

All in the vain name of “democracy,” too.

news.originalContent:

Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will call plays for the team, come hell or high water.

That’s the message coach Jim Harbaugh sent Wednesday when he confirmed McDaniel would continue calling plays coming off the team’s bye week.

The Chargers evaluated the team over the last few days and remain comfortable with McDaniel leading the offense. But as the team enters Week 8 with an 0-6 record, LA hasn’t made any notable changes to a struggling squad.

But the NFL’s lone winless team appears to be content in sticking with the staff laid out in the offseason.

“We’re very confident in Mike and his talent, work ethic and ability. And continue to be,” Harbaugh told reporters Wednesday.

It is important to note Harbaugh has never called plays throughout his tenure as a head coach. But if McDaniel continues calling plays for the Chargers, what changes can they make to turn things around?

Evidently, the Chargers believe the self-scouting done over the bye week will suffice upon their return to the field, but things look bleak for LA. Their next challenge is squaring off against the Rams on Sunday, which doesn’t bode well for their chances of securing their first win of the season.

However, Harbaugh and the coaching staff remain adamant about the team’s progress week in and week out regardless of the Chargers’ abysmal record.
